claims.text: What the strip looks like Normal sinus rhythm in every way except the rate, which is under 60 bpm.
P waves: normal sinus P waves, one before every QRS, as in NSR
PR interval: normal and constant, as in NSR
ST segment and T waves: normal, as in NSR
U waves: prominent U waves in the precordial leads are a common finding
claims.quote: Note the prominent U waves in the precordial leads, a common finding in sinus bradycardia.

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Physiologic: young children, adolescents and young adults (especially athletes), and during sleep
claims.quote: Slower rates (sinus bradycardia) occur in young children, adolescents, and young adults, particularly athletes, and during sleep.

claims.text: Vagal: increased vagal tone (e.g., athletes) or vagal stimulation (e.g., pain)
claims.quote: Increased vagal tone (e.g. athletes) Vagal stimulation (e.g. pain)

claims.text: Disease: inferior MI, sinus node disease, hypothyroidism, hypothermia, anorexia nervosa, hyperkalemia or hypermagnesemia, brainstem herniation (Cushing reflex), myocarditis
claims.quote: Inferior myocardial infarction Sinus node disease Hypothyroidism Hypothermia Anorexia nervosa Electrolyte abnormalities – hyperkalaemia, hypermagnesaemia Brainstem herniation (the Cushing reflex) Myocarditis

claims.text: Drugs and toxins: beta blockers, verapamil and diltiazem, digoxin, clonidine and dexmedetomidine, amiodarone, opioids, GABA-ergic agents (barbiturates, benzodiazepines, baclofen, GHB), organophosphate poisoning
claims.quote: Beta-blockers Calcium-channel blockers (verapamil & diltiazem) Digoxin Central alpha-2 agonists (clonidine & dexmedetomidine) Amiodarone Opiates GABA-ergic agents (barbiturates, benzodiazepines, baclofen, GHB) Organophosphate poisoning

claims.text: Symptoms May cause none; when it compromises perfusion: dyspnea, chest discomfort, presyncope or syncope
claims.quote: Arrhythmia and conduction disturbances may be asymptomatic or cause palpitations (sensation of skipped beats or rapid or forceful beats), symptoms of hemodynamic compromise (eg, dyspnea, chest discomfort, presyncope, syncope), or cardiac arrest.

claims.text: Treatment Asymptomatic, low-risk bradycardia needs no treatment
claims.quote: Asymptomatic arrhythmias without serious risks do not require treatment even if they worsen.

claims.text: Otherwise treatment is directed at the cause
Unstable or needing urgent treatment (temporizing): transcutaneous pacing, atropine and/or isoproterenol
claims.quote: Bradycardia: Transcutaneous pacing, atropine, and/or isoproterenol
